podcast.title: Discovery of Blur (1990)
podcast.body: In 1990, Food Records, a small independent label, discovered the young band Blur, with whom they signed their first record deal. "En 1990 una pequeña discográfica independiente llamada Food Records, se descubrió una joven banda que se llamaría Blur"

srcs.episode: El BRIT POP como negocio discográfico

podcast.title: Acquisition by EMI
podcast.body: By mid-1992, EMI became a shareholder in Food Records, significantly boosting resources and promotion for Blur's second album. Following Blur's immense success with "Parklife," EMI fully acquired 100% of Food Records, eager to secure one of the UK's biggest bands under its complete ownership.

podcast.title: Acquisition by EMI
podcast.body: Shortly after the release of Blur's debut album, *Leisure*, EMI acquired Food Records specifically to secure the band Blur. "poco después del lanzamiento del Laser, Emmy compro Food Records precisamente para poder hacerse con Blur."

srcs.episode: El BRIT POP como negocio discográfico

podcast.title: Blur Discovery and Renaming
podcast.body: Food, an indie label, discovered the band Seymour and successfully persuaded them to change their name to Blur, contributing to their rise as one of the most important new bands in the UK by 1994. "Then there was a group called Seymour, who attracted the attention of an indie label called Food. They convinced them to change their name to Blur."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Britpop Success with Tiny Label
podcast.body: Food was a "tiny little label" that signed Blur, enabling them to achieve mainstream success during the Britpop scene of the mid-1990s. This case highlights how, in the UK, even small independent labels could launch major acts into the national spotlight due to the specific characteristics of the British music industry. "People forget that blur made it big while on a tiny little label called Food."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Blur Contract
podcast.body: Food Records, a small independent record label based in London, signed Blur early in their career, offering them a contract for one album and some singles. They quickly began to back the band, releasing "She's So High" in October 1990.

podcast.title: Pillar of 90s European Alternative Music
podcast.body: Food Records is identified as one of the great pillars of 90s alternative music in Europe. Producer Alan Moulder is closely associated with this label. "Food Records que es uno de los grandes pilares de la música alternativa de los 90 en Europa."
